referents.why: 'Him' (auton) is the one the crowd calls to be crucified: Jesus. Jesus is not in this verse's candidate list, which offers only Pilate and Barabbas.
Implied 'you' of the imperative is the one the cry is spoken to: Pilate, who asked the question in Mrk.15.12. Singular morphology fits one addressee.

links.why: The command is the object of 'cried out'. Grammar nesting kept beside the content link.
R1: 'cried out' is a clause of calling out that introduces what is said: a single command, so the said clause itself.

groups.why: Frame cl0; part cl1, the command. Addressee is Pilate, the one the cry is spoken to (cl1s). The sender, the crowd, is not a candidate, so it is omitted.
groups.category: cry turn with sender not in candidates

cant_tell.what: sender of the cry (the crowd, subject of cl0)
cant_tell.why: The subject 'they' of cl0 has no slot, and the crowd is not a candidate.
Not offered as a candidate in this verse.
